'''Jean Bertoin''' (born 25 May 1961) is a French mathematician. He is professor at the [[University of Zurich]] since 2011.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=Jean Bertoin (CV) |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/short-CV.pdf |publisher=European Academy of Sciences |access-date=29 March 2025 |date=2024}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Bertoin was born in [[Lyon]] and completed his undergraduate studies at the [[École Normale Supérieure of St Cloud]].<ref name="bertoin1">{{cite web |title=Jean Bertoin |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/jean-bertoin/member/ |publisher=European Academy of Sciences |access-date=29 March 2025 |date=13 April 2022}}</ref> He received his doctorate from [[University of Paris VI]] in 1987, having been advised by [[Marc Yor]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=69222}}</ref>

==Career==
Bertoin is a specialist in [[probability theory]]. His research deals with [[Lévy process]]es, [[Brownian motion]], [[branching processes]], random fragmentation, and coalescence processes.<ref name=bertoin1 />

In 1988, Bertoin became a researcher at [[CNRS]], and was appointed Professor at [[Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University]] in 1992.<ref name=bertoin1 /> In the early 1990s he began a collaboration with [[Ron Doney]] on the topic of conditioned [[random walks]], with the pair co-writing six papers between 1994 and 1997.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chaumont |first1=Loïc |last2=Kyprianou |first2=Andreas E. |title=A Lifetime of Excursions Through Random Walks and Lévy Processes |journal=Progress in Probability |date=2021 |volume=78 |page=4 |url=https://people.bath.ac.uk/ak257/DoneyFest.pdf |access-date=29 March 2025}}</ref>

Bertoin has received numerous awards, including the CNRS Bronze Medal (1992), the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] (1996), and the Thérèse Gautier Prize (2015). He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] (2002) and [[European Congress of Mathematics|ECM]] (2012), and elected a corresponding member of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name=bertoin1 />

His doctoral students include [[Grégory Miermont]].
